# KBD Constraints

Constraints the artifact-refiner QA gate validates for every change from
`phase-codex-plugin-distribution-and-ci` onward. Each completed change is checked
against these before archiving (`/refine-validate <change-id>`); a violation marks
the change BLOCKED.

## C-01 — Generated artifacts must be in sync

Any source consumed by a generator must have its generated outputs regenerated
and committed before the owning parent phase completes or its final phase
commit is pushed. A parent phase may name one later reconciliation change to batch this
work when several sibling changes edit the same generated surface; every earlier
change must identify that reconciliation change in persisted execution evidence,
and none may claim distribution certification in the interim. The reconciliation
change must run the generator twice, prove byte-identical tracked hashes, and run
the applicable drift validators before phase certification. A deferral that
crosses the parent-phase boundary, omits the named owner, or reaches parent-phase
certification, final commit, or push without regenerated outputs is a violation.

Also generator inputs, from the integration contract (v1.0.0) onward:
`shared/launchagents/*.plist` and `shared/systemd/*.service|.timer|.path` feed
`shared/services.manifest.json` via `scripts/generate-service-manifest.mjs`
(seam 3 of `docs/integration-contract.md`). Any change that edits, adds, or
deletes one of those templates MUST regenerate the manifest and pass
`npm run check:services-manifest` in the same change. The manifest is generated;
hand-editing it is a violation.

Specifically: after touching `.claude-plugin/*`, `.mcp.json`,
`hooks/hooks.json`, or `scripts/build-codex-plugin.js`, `npm run validate:codex`
MUST pass (no drift, valid manifest + marketplace) in the same change because
those files directly define the generator or already-generated plugin surface.
Hand-editing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` or
`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is always a violation — they are generated.

## C-02 — No committed secrets

No API keys, tokens, or passwords in tracked files. Env vars and `${VAR:-default}`
placeholders only; real secret values live in the environment or user-local config
(`~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.bash_profile`), never in the repo. Localhost dev
credentials that are already an established repo convention (e.g. surrealdb
`root/root`, the forge localhost dev token) are exempt.

## C-03 — Docs updated with surface changes

A change that alters the Codex plugin surface (manifest fields, marketplace
schema, MCP servers, hooks, install flow) must update `docs/codex-plugin.md` and,
where relevant, the CLAUDE.md "Codex CLI Integration" section in the same change.

## C-04 — Generators stay idempotent

`node scripts/build-codex-plugin.js` run twice must produce byte-identical output.
`--check` must exit non-zero on drift or invalid artifacts. New generator features
(e.g. source-type knobs) must preserve idempotency for a fixed input.

## C-05 — Scripts under launchd are bash 3.2 compatible

Any script that can be invoked by a launchd agent (macOS `/bin/bash` is 3.2) must
avoid `mapfile` / `declare -A`. Test with `/bin/bash script.sh`, not just `bash`.

## QA and local review coverage

Every change requires deterministic artifact validation followed by independent
cumulative diff review before archive and final certification, including small
and documentation-only changes. Missing tools or explicit skip flags record
`pending_review`; they do not imply a passing gate. Final certification requires
a completed review receipt or the explicit signed waiver required by the current
`kbd-execute` contract. Generated-output deferral is limited to C-01 above.

# Governing-policy conflicts block dependent work until acknowledged

Phase: issue-195-closeout · Change: i195-01-policy-conflict-ack

## Why

Issue #195 acceptance 2 requires a governing-policy conflict to be surfaced before dependent execution. Today `method-context.mjs` lists conflicts but `status` (line 128) and `--require-resolved` (line 182) ignore them, so a recovered session can proceed past the conflict. This repository's own CLAUDE.md:102 / AGENTS.md:104 compiler-check exception triggers it once VLBV is selected.

## What changes

- Reuse the existing signed decision surface: an acknowledgement is a decision whose summary is `KBD-POLICY-ACK {"phaseId","path","sha256","issue","note"}`, recorded with `prometheus kbd decision record` and replaced through `--supersedes` (same pattern as `KBD-METHOD`, method-context.mjs:70-80). No new event kind, CLI command or schema.
- A conflict is `acknowledged` only when exactly one current (non-superseded) ack matches phaseId, path and the file's current SHA-256. A changed policy file therefore re-raises the conflict.
- Any unacknowledged conflict sets `status: "CONFLICT"` (blockers still win: BLOCKED > CONFLICT > RESOLVED_REFERENCES); `--require-resolved` exits 2 for both BLOCKED and CONFLICT. Each conflict entry gains `acknowledged` and `ackDecisionId`.
- reanchor.sh prints a blocking line naming each unacknowledged conflict; kbd-handoff.sh includes `policyConflicts` in its method summary. references/method-context.md documents the payload, the recording command and the trust model.
- Operator-owned policy files are never edited. Control is described honestly: canonical Decision state carries no actor, so acknowledgement authority equals the existing KBD-METHOD trust model (instruction-level; not a new guarantee).

## Scope

- `skills/process/kbd-process-orchestrator/shared/method-context.mjs`
- `skills/process/prometheus-context-bootstrap/assets/hooks/reanchor.sh`
- `skills/process/kbd-process-orchestrator/skills/kbd-handoff/kbd-handoff.sh`
- `skills/process/kbd-process-orchestrator/references/method-context.md`

## Constraints

- Recalled lesson: "`kbd-apply mark-done` updates the task flag but does not synchronize the canonical KBD ledger" — close tasks only with kbd-apply begin-task/end-task.
- Implementation first (CLAUDE.md, highest precedence): no tests, builds or checks before every planned production change in the phase is complete; acceptance is gathered only at the final boundary owned by i195-03.
- Exclusions: #184 exit semantics, #185 trusted tool admission, the operator-authority trust model, a generic shell fence, and any edit to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md policy text.

# One identical selected-method core in all stage skills

Phase: issue-195-closeout · Change: i195-02-single-method-reference · Depends on: i195-01-policy-conflict-ack

## Why

The `## Selected-method recovery and authority` section is hand-copied into 11 stage skills (two byte variants today, differing by one trailing blank line). Issue #195 acceptance 5 needs source, generated and installed surfaces to keep the same semantics; copies drift.

## What changes

- Replace the section in the 11 stage skills (kbd-assess, kbd-child-exit, kbd-execute, kbd-handoff, kbd-init, kbd-new-child, kbd-next-child, kbd-pause, kbd-plan, kbd-resume, kbd-spec) with one identical short core (below) that keeps the load-bearing rules inline and links `references/method-context.md` for the rest. A bare link is rejected: a model may not open it.
- Add `scripts/check-selected-method-core.mjs` (wired as `npm run check:selected-method`) that fails when any stage skill's section differs byte-for-byte from the canonical core or is missing.
- Regenerate and commit tracked outputs in the same change: `npm run build:distribution` (dist/plugins/claude/**, dist/plugins/codex/**, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, .agents/plugins/marketplace.json) and `npm run generate:skills-index` (SKILLS.md).

Canonical core:

```markdown
## Selected-method recovery and authority

Before dependent work, run `shared/method-context.mjs --project <project-root> --phase <canonical-phase-id> --write` from the resolved orchestrator root (or read the phase-local `method-context.md` when Node is unavailable) and act on its `status`:

- `RESOLVED_REFERENCES` — continue with the recovered method, contract and stage authority; preserve the same references in role inputs, dispatch and handoff read order.
- `BLOCKED` — a method decision, contract, calibration or supersession is missing or changed; resolve it explicitly. Prior commands, memory and tool inventories are not fresh authority.
- `CONFLICT` — governing host policy conflicts with the selected method. Stop before dependent work and show the conflict; continue only after the operator records a `KBD-POLICY-ACK` decision for that file's current hash. Never rewrite operator-owned policy.

For selected VLBV, define acceptance before generation and finish the whole agreed value phase before any generated-code verification; tasks, hours, commits, reviewer requests and compiler problems create no boundary. Preserve original evidence, consumed budgets and unresolved effects across resume and supersession; reconcile an uncertain effect before any retry. Full rules: `references/method-context.md`.
```

## Scope

# Author and run the issue #195 closeout evidence; close honestly

Phase: issue-195-closeout · Change: i195-03-delivery-qualification · Depends on: i195-01-policy-conflict-ack, i195-02-single-method-reference

## Why

VER-001 and VER-003 are stubs (scripts/tests/lib/kbd-194-196-sessions.mjs:314-316), so #195 acceptance 4 and 6 have no evidence; Codex and OpenCode were never exercised; the session driver leaves PROMETHEUS_PLUGIN_ROOT unset. This change owns all test authoring and the single final boundary, after changes 01 and 02 are complete.

## What changes

- Task 1 runs only after every production task of changes 01 and 02 is done (host policy: implementation first).
- Session driver isolation: set a scratch PROMETHEUS_PLUGIN_ROOT for every harness. Add an OpenCode harness: `opencode run --format json --standalone` with scratch XDG_CONFIG_HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME, OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1, OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1, preceded by an isolation preflight that confirms config and auth resolve under the scratch roots; otherwise the scenario is NOT_EXERCISED (unsupported isolation), never run against real config.
- Implement VER-001 and VER-003 bodies in place of stub(); add CON-001..003, REF-001, SRF-001, SRF-002 and register them so the driver iterates this phase's contract.
- Task 2 runs the boundary packet once; fixes go in coherent batches with one confirming rerun, within the adopted budget.
- Task 3: cross-model review of the cumulative diff (judge not Claude-family; label recorded honestly), `npm run validate:strict`, `npm run check:distribution`, protected-test certification from the committed candidate.
- Task 4: typed canonical closure of this phase with the six claims kept distinct and no successor; record a partial disposition for issues-194-195-196 that references this phase; draft the #195 acceptance-to-evidence comment. Posting the comment and closing the issue are outward-facing and need explicit owner authorization at that time.

## Scope

- `scripts/tests/lib/kbd-194-196-sessions.mjs`
- `scripts/tests/lib/kbd-195-closeout.mjs`
- `scripts/tests/kbd-194-196.integration.mjs`
- `.kbd-orchestrator/phases/issue-195-closeout/evidence/**`
- `.kbd-orchestrator/phases/issue-195-closeout/review/final/**`
- `.kbd-orchestrator/phases/issue-195-closeout/closure-report.md`

## Constraints

- Recalled lesson: "A CRITICAL shipped despite all per-change gates passing … the installer never applied the Codex memory setting" — surface checks observe the installer-dispatched payload, never source text alone.
- Recalled lesson: "`kbd-apply mark-done` updates the task flag but does not synchronize the canonical KBD ledger" — close tasks only with kbd-apply begin-task/end-task.
- Implementation first (CLAUDE.md, highest precedence): no tests, builds or checks before every planned production change in the phase is complete; acceptance is gathered only at the final boundary owned by i195-03.
- Exclusions: #184 exit semantics, #185 trusted tool admission, the operator-authority trust model, a generic shell fence, and any edit to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md policy text.
